IN-2026-HB1001.s: The bill became law and changes several housing and building rules for cities, towns, and counties. It changes how some housing money can be used, limits certain permit fees and delays, and sets new reporting and review steps for local housing rules. It also changes some building code and flood plain rules, and updates how some housing authority projects and bonds can be handled.

IN-2026-HB1003.s: This law creates a task force to study farm-related issues and changes how some state rules are renewed. It also changes, combines, or ends several state boards and commissions, and it changes some funds tied to them. The law moves fire prevention and building safety work and rules to the Department of Homeland Security, changes some building safety laws, and includes an appropriation, which is money set aside by the state.

IN-2026-HB1004.s: The law makes many changes to Indiana school rules, including school accounting, state board duties, graduation plans, internet use policies, excused absences, and AED requirements. It also changes rules for charter schools, teacher contracts, teacher recruitment and retention, and some reporting and grant programs. It became Public Law 74 on March 4, 2026.

IN-2026-HB1031.s: Indiana law changes how hospitals keep blood or tissue for death investigations and updates the training rules for coroners and deputy coroners. It also changes how death investigations are done. A coroner or deputy coroner who does a death investigation or signs a death certificate without the required training commits a Class B misdemeanor, and the county can seek back training costs if the training is not finished on time.

IN-2026-HB1038.s: The law changes some gaming rules and gives the horse racing commission fewer satellite site licenses to issue. It also requires Allen, DeKalb, and Steuben counties to put a casino vote on the 2026 ballot and lets the state gaming commission award a new inland casino license in one of those counties if voters approve it. An approved casino applicant must plan to invest at least $500 million and pay $150 million, with most of that going to the state and part set aside for local areas affected by a closed riverboat or casino.

IN-2026-HB1052.s: The bill changes several state rules on racing, gambling, alcohol, tobacco, and some permits. It would change when racing licenses can be taken away or denied, add sports wagering holders to the self-ban program, set rules and fines for sweepstakes games, and update rules for beer, wine, and tobacco sales. It also allows a few new local alcohol permits and treats antique firearms differently under some handgun sale rules. The bill became Public Law 153 on March 12, 2026.

IN-2026-HB1062.s: Sets rules for wake boarding and wake surfing on public freshwater lakes and on small lakes. It also creates a penalty for breaking those rules. The bill became Public Law 154.

IN-2026-HB1092.s: The law changes several child support, adoption, and child welfare rules. It lets Indiana withhold some mobile sports betting withdrawals from people who owe child support, adds ways to pay child support, and changes how paternity orders can be handled. It also adds checks and limits for some child care licenses, requires more details in some adoption petitions, and sets rules for caseworkers who want to interview a child at school.

IN-2026-HB1115.s: The law changes rules for homeowners associations in Indiana. It limits fees for sale or refinance statements, bars fees for account statements and other covered HOA services, and requires boards to give at least four days' written notice for board meetings with an agenda. It also lets members attend meetings online, sets limits on how HOA rules can be changed, and allows fines only under a set fee schedule with notice to the homeowner. The bill became Public Law 155 on March 12, 2026.

IN-2026-HB1116.s: Indiana’s law bars virtual currency kiosks from operating in the state. If someone breaks the rule, the attorney general can take action under consumer sales law, and a person who knowingly or intentionally breaks it may have to give up the fees charged to users or the kiosk itself. The attorney general may also sue the kiosk operator, and the property owner if they knowingly allowed the kiosk to stay there.

IN-2026-HB1145.s: The law lets some members of the state excise police, gaming agent, gaming control officer, and conservation enforcement officers' retirement plan choose a joint and survivor payment option for their retirement money. It also provides a one-time extra payment, called a thirteenth check, in 2026 for certain members, participants, or beneficiaries in five state retirement plans, including teachers, public employees, and state police. It became Public Law 79.

IN-2026-HB1165.s: Indiana law changes several rules on animal-related crimes and liability. It removes some liability when a person removes a domestic animal from a motor vehicle, raises some penalties for animal offenses, and adds a defense for someone not involved who is attacked by a law enforcement animal. It also updates animal law definitions, says animal cruelty rules apply to non-nuisance rodents, and lets certain acts count as factors that can increase a sentence.

IN-2026-HB1192.s: Indiana seed law would be updated to include several state rules, and some rules would be repealed. It would also make small wording and format changes to fit the new law. The bill became Public Law 82 on March 4, 2026.

IN-2026-HB1193.s: The law changes what the Indiana civil rights commission can do in civil rights cases. It bars the commission from representing a private person in court, lets it represent only the state, and requires some complaints to be sent first to another state or federal agency with authority over them. It also changes the rules for some discrimination claims, who files certain court cases, and when attorney’s fees may be paid.

IN-2026-HB1200.s: The law changes many BMV rules, including license plate design, driver and permit application details, and some license renewal rules. It also lets a rear-view camera count instead of a rear mirror in some vehicles, changes age and testing rules for drivers, and adds new rules for commercial driver licenses. It also bans the state road agency from using variable speed limits or electronic variable speed limit signs.

IN-2026-HB1210.s: This law makes many changes to local taxes, property tax rules, and how some local government data is reported. It also changes rules for notices, land assessment, mobile home title transfers, and some school and fire service funding. It affects local governments, taxpayers, school corporations, and some property owners, and it became Public Law 157 on March 12, 2026.

IN-2026-HB1249.s: The law changes several criminal rules, including penalties for operating while intoxicated, battery against some school and health care workers, and dangerous gun possession by a child. It adds some OWI rules for watercraft, allows some people to ask for a limited driving privilege after an initial hearing, and lets people get good time credit while serving certain OWI sentences. It also changes some rules for fatal crash testing, drone-based harassment, and public reports about railroad deaths. The bill became Public Law 158 on March 12, 2026.

IN-2026-HB1257.s: Indiana Public Law 84 changes several child services rules. It adds members to the child fatality review committee, lets a court allow postadoption contact when a child is at least 1 year old, and expands what the Department of Child Services must report and share about child deaths, near deaths, and child abuse or neglect cases. It also changes when the department must assess abuse reports and when it may provide services in child in need of services cases.

IN-2026-HB1258.s: Changes and tightens the state rules for what counts as a crime of violence. It also updates the labels for people who are convicted of, charged with, or arrested for those crimes, and drops the repeat violent arrestee rule. The law adds two gun offenses with two prior offenses to the violence list and makes other matching changes.

IN-2026-HB1260.s: The law changes several insurance rules in Indiana. It requires reports of suspected insurance fraud to go to the insurance department or the National Insurance Crime Bureau, and gives some people protection from civil or criminal liability when they report it. It also changes notice rules for insurance nonrenewal, data fees, some insurance coverage rules, and several other insurance policies and programs. It became Public Law 86 on March 4, 2026.

IN-2026-HB1266.s: This law makes many changes to Indiana education rules. It updates math teaching plans, teacher pay rules, school board membership, summer school, school choice scholarships, and career and technical education. It also requires new reviews and reports for some school and college programs and sets steps for the state to join a federal tax credit scholarship program.

IN-2026-HB1268.s: The bill became law and adds two voting members to the Indiana defense task force, plus the Indiana National Guard adjutant general, or a designee, as a nonvoting member. It also sets yearly report deadlines on defense spending priorities and asks the state defense development office to consider those priorities when it builds its budget. The bill also directs the Indiana Economic Development Corporation and an operating partner to run the federal Unmanned Aircraft System Test Site program in Indiana.

IN-2026-HB1277.s: Changes how Indiana Medicaid home and community-based waiver services are managed and paid for. It would require more review of service paperwork, let some Medicaid members pick their care coordinator, set timelines for requests to raise service units, and direct the state to seek federal approval for a new assisted living waiver and other Medicaid changes. It also changes some home health payment rules, updates a drug-compounding term, and sets a 9-month deadline for certain estate recovery claims.

IN-2026-HB1278.s: Indiana law now says the Indiana State Nurses Association must send the governor a list of qualified nurses when there is a board of nursing vacancy or when a term ends. It also lets schools that have run an eligible nursing program for at least five years raise enrollment at any rate they think is right. The changes affect nurse board appointments and nursing schools in Indiana.

IN-2026-HB1286.s: A person in a protective order case would have to tell the court about any military protective orders between the two sides. The court could also consider a military protective order used to protect the person asking for the order. It would also treat some Canadian court protection orders as valid foreign protection orders.

IN-2026-HB1342.s: The law asks the legislative council to send the issue to an interim study committee, which is a temporary group that looks into a topic. That group would study whether county officials should use certain steps when setting up or changing county commissioner districts.

IN-2026-HB1343.s: The law updates rules for public safety, county jails, boating, veterans' services, and the Indiana National Guard. It lets the training board pick an executive director, allows some out-of-state police training to count, and raises the jail copay limit to up to $30. It also changes rules for military family relief aid, adds a National Guard military police force, and sets new rules for some water vessels and armory property. It was signed into law on March 4, 2026.

IN-2026-HB1360.s: Indiana Public Law 97 would change how public records requests are handled by state and local agencies. It lets agencies use an online portal with tools to check if the requester is a real person and to confirm address and Indiana residency, and it lets them flag requests that look like automated, phishing, or data-scraping activity. It also lets agencies delay or deny some requests in limited cases, charge extra fees to nonresidents or out-of-state entities, and give priority to Indiana residents and certain kinds of request uses.

IN-2026-HB1368.s: The law requires utilities to accept certain payment methods from the Department of Natural Resources for service at state-owned property, and it limits how much a utility can restrict the size or number of payments for one bill. It also lets the department ask for one combined bill for a property, unless the utility cannot do that because of billing or other limits. The law gives the Natural Resources Commission power to regulate Class VI underground injection wells and sets rules for storing carbon dioxide in Indiana, with special treatment for the carbon sequestration pilot project.

IN-2026-HB1406.s: Enacted as Public Law 162, this measure changes several tax and budget rules in Indiana. It requires some counties to mail property tax statements to all property owners, even when no tax is due, and it adds new reporting, tax credit, and library budget review rules. It also changes some local tax powers, rules for certain nonprofit hospital property, and several state economic development and fraud-prevention programs.

IN-2026-HB1408.s: The law changes how state data is shared, including giving the General Assembly access to some Management Performance Hub data and its yearly data report. It also changes some rules for Ivy Tech, including campus planning, building use reviews, trustee and campus board duties, and yearly reports on programs, students, and job market results. It also sets rules for teen social media use and says breaking those rules is a deceptive act.

IN-2026-HB1423.s: Creates a new Indianapolis public education corporation and board to handle certain school and tax duties in Indianapolis. It changes who can approve some charter schools in the city area, sets up new tax and debt funds, and lets the corporation use some school tax revenue. It also says the corporation may issue bonds or take on debt only in a set time window and only if the Indianapolis school board first approves it.

IN-2026-HB1424.s: Allows homestead vendors and small farm vendors to sell certain foods, including some meat products, from their property or at farmers markets. It also limits state and local health rules and licensing for these sellers to what federal law requires, while still allowing health officials to look into foodborne illness complaints. The bill sets rules for labels, shipping, delivery, handling, cold storage, and some building and fire safety rules for the places where the food is sold. It became Public Law 163 on March 12, 2026.

IN-2026-SB1.s: Enacted law creates an Indiana rural health transformation fund, with spending on that money reviewed by a budget committee and reported on twice a year. It changes SNAP rules by banning candy and soft drinks with SNAP benefits, ending expanded categorical eligibility, and setting new income and immigration checks. It also changes Medicaid and the Healthy Indiana Plan by setting timing rules for reviews and enrollment, adding income and work rules, and adding some copays for emergency room use when care is not an emergency.

IN-2026-SB119.s: The law adds places with shows or programs mainly for children under 18 to the list of places where certain sex offenders may not work or volunteer. It also bars a serious sex offender from entering those places and renames “inappropriate communication with a child” as “sexual grooming,” with a broader rule for repeated contact meant to make a child less resistant to sex. It also says “computer network” includes cell phones.

IN-2026-SB139.s: Indiana Public Law 69 would exempt a woman who is breastfeeding from jury duty. It also sets requirements for getting that exemption.

IN-2026-SB14.s: Indiana’s pension law makes several changes to public worker retirement plans. It changes how pay is counted for some retirement benefits, adds rules for buying service credit, and changes how some retirement money is handled. It also creates a new retiree health benefit trust and raises the lump sum death benefit for some 1977 fund members. The bill became Public Law 104 on March 5, 2026.

IN-2026-SB140.s: The law expands Indiana’s intimidation rule to treat posting a person’s personal information on social media as a threat if it is meant to cause injury, property damage, or a crime against that person. It also raises the penalty for intimidation when the target is a legislator.

IN-2026-SB148.s: Starting July 1, 2027, the Indiana crime guns task force would add LaPorte County and Porter County to its area. It also sets the number of members needed for a quorum, which is the minimum needed to do official business, and explains how the task force can act if there is a tie vote. The bill became Public Law 70.

IN-2026-SB164.s: Requires the Indiana Department of Agriculture to study whether community or urban microfarm zones could work statewide. The department must send a report with its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2027. It became Public Law 71.

IN-2026-SB169.s: The law reorganizes Indiana’s consumer lending rules into a new part of the state code. It moves laws on first-lien mortgage loans, small loans, mortgage rescue fraud, home loan practices, and the Uniform Consumer Credit Code into Title 37. It also updates related cross-references and the layout of the laws to match the state’s drafting rules.

IN-2026-SB171.s: This law changes some adoption and child welfare rules in Indiana. It requires child services to notify the court about an adoption petition in certain CHINS cases, allows adoption consent to be given after birth by an attorney, in person, or by video, and lets courts grant post-adoption contact at age 12 months instead of 2 years. It also changes how placement changes are handled for children in child welfare cases, including notice, court orders, and limits on changing a child's placement while an adoption petition is pending.

IN-2026-SB179.s: Becoming Public Law 147 on March 12, 2026, this measure lets the Indiana Department of Transportation take on some federal environmental law duties and agree to go to federal court for those duties. It also changes rules for local road and bridge grants, single-trip overweight truck permits, and how real estate can be described using the Indiana Plane Coordinate System. The law also lets counties in some cases add a vehicle excise tax or wheel tax after December 31, 2026, and changes township capital improvement plan rules.

IN-2026-SB180.s: The law changes several health care rules. It lowers some training rules for home health aides, changes education and permit rules for dental hygienists and respiratory care workers, and lets the dental board set more rules for people who fail the licensure test three times. It also lets current and former police officers and firefighters seek medical benefits from their employer for job-related injuries or illness without first filing a workers' compensation claim, and it repeals one old penalty in state health law.

IN-2026-SB185.s: The law changes rules for tobacco, vaping, alcohol, and flavored nitrous oxide in Indiana. It adds limits for tobacco sales certificates, including where a shop may be located, what must be on an application, and when a certificate can be suspended or taken away. It also adds rules and penalties for e-liquid and vapor products, changes some tobacco and minor-entry violation thresholds, and treats selling alcohol without a permit as a racketeering-related violation.

IN-2026-SB189.s: This law changes the process for out-of-network health care payment disputes. It requires quick written notice after a request for independent dispute resolution, lets a health carrier send notice after 25 or more qualified disputes in 90 days, and requires the carrier, provider, and facility to try to work out a deal in good faith. It also bars health carriers from charging a facility or provider an administrative fee or penalty tied to care that involves an out-of-network provider.

IN-2026-SB199.s: This law changes how some education rules are handled in Indiana. It changes the makeup of a review panel for school sports, asks the state education chief to report on civic learning and paid leave issues, and requires a review of schools with low reading scores and of accrediting agencies for state colleges. It also says some state college degree programs that federal law calls low earning must get state approval to keep running.

IN-2026-SB2.s: Indiana’s bail rules would change for most offenses other than murder. A court could deny bail if the state shows the person is dangerous and that no release conditions would reasonably protect others or the community, and it would add steps for a bail hearing. It would also let courts keep cash bail to pay certain costs if the defendant agreed to that in writing.

IN-2026-SB200.s: The law changes some school vendor contracts signed, changed, or renewed after June 30, 2026. It says some parts of those contracts about liability protection, state law choice, and automatic renewal are void and cannot be enforced. It also lets certain youth groups file a grievance with the state education department if a public school will not let them share information with students, and it requires schools to give military recruiters the same access they give to colleges for certain student information.

IN-2026-SB204.s: The law changes several education rules in Indiana. It makes it easier for some charter school teachers to get a regular teaching license, changes some pay rules for teachers, and updates or ends several reporting requirements for colleges. It also lets some students in health training programs object to required shots for religious reasons and changes rules for degree program closures and transfer credits.

IN-2026-SB214.s: The bill updates how the Department of Workforce Development handles several unemployment and job service rules, including experience accounts, reporting, payment rates, seasonal and part-time workers, work searches, claims, hearings, and notice. It also changes the department’s role in cooperation agreements and when it may issue a civil penalty for unauthorized postsecondary proprietary schools. The bill was signed into law as Public Law 121.

IN-2026-SB222.s: The law changes how Indiana's family and social services agency handles some health and care programs. It makes the 9-8-8 crisis line and mobile crisis teams first responders, updates who can provide Medicaid services, and changes several aging and disability offices and names. It also affects some home health agencies, certified peer workers, and the micro facility pilot program.

IN-2026-SB224.s: The law changes several rules for the Department of Natural Resources and the natural resources commission, including how some procedures work and how river basin commissions are set up. It also removes the hometown Indiana grant program, changes boating, wakeboard, and off-road vehicle rules, and raises the dollar limits tied to some accident reporting steps. It adds new limits on when landowners can be held liable for injuries to people using land for recreation, and it removes the penalty for acting as a hunting guide without a guide license.

IN-2026-SB225.s: The law changes the rules for ambulatory outpatient surgical centers by removing the requirement that certain surgeons have hospital privileges. It also sets new limits on hospital medical debt collection, including state review of hospital compliance, notices to patients, and penalties for hospitals, debt collectors, or other third parties that try to collect while a hospital is noncompliant. The law also bars liens on a patient’s primary residence for medical debt when the patient is acting in good faith and requires hospitals to give advance notice before closing or reducing a service line.

IN-2026-SB226.s: The law lets the Indiana Department of Administration manage some state buying and contracting in a new way called category management, where similar purchases are grouped together. It also changes how a state agency picks its purchasing representative and requires the department to run an outside check program for state contracts. State agencies must send a yearly buying plan to the department and the budget agency, and a separate rule on the Indiana War Memorials Commission's contracting power is repealed.

IN-2026-SB227.s: The law makes the Indiana State Police the main state agency to coordinate counter-drone work allowed by federal law. It would apply only after the federal government gives that power and the governor posts a notice in the Indiana Register. The state police could pick local police agencies to join the program if they meet federal training and readiness rules, and could choose Indianapolis for a pilot project. It also says drone blocking steps may be used only when federal law clearly allows them.

IN-2026-SB239.s: Indiana law now requires the education department to publish a list of business and industry partners that give honors employment plus seal students guaranteed incentives. It also changes rules for converting public schools into charter schools, including some cases where more than one school can be converted and one charter can cover more than one school. The law also changes rules for some charter school agreements and school building closures, and it requires parent notice when a student may not be on track in math.

IN-2026-SB241.s: The law changes some water and sewer utility rules in Indiana. It raises the customer limit for a conservancy district to leave state utility oversight from less than 2,000 to less than 3,000 customers, and it adds new rules for special contracts tied to workforce housing in rural areas. It also lets some utilities pass through certain chemical and power cost changes more often, and it says some connection fees for eligible workforce housing can be reduced or waived under set rules.

IN-2026-SB243.s: Indiana law changes several state taxes and tax rules, including income tax, sales tax, cigarette tax, fuel and alcohol taxes, and aircraft taxes. It also changes how the state tax department can send notices, how some tax debts and audits are handled, and how tax credit and withholding rules work for things like gambling winnings, ABLE accounts, research costs, and adoption. The law also adds rules for certain sales tax enforcement cases and for who can be held responsible for trust fund taxes, which are taxes a business holds and sends to the state.

IN-2026-SB246.s: The law requires certain names and other details to be hidden in criminal court records for child victims, child witnesses, and some other people. When a name is hidden, courts must use an unnamed label like "Child Witness No. 1" instead of initials or a family label. It became Public Law 129 on March 5, 2026.

IN-2026-SB254.s: Changes how Ivy Tech Community College is run by shifting and combining some board and campus board duties. It lets campus board members represent an employer in the campus area and has the campus board help name people to fill vacancies, make plan and budget recommendations, and work with the campus chancellor. It also tells the Indiana Economic Development Corporation to set up a school-to-job research program and a plan for sharing that data by December 1, 2026. The bill became Public Law 130.

IN-2026-SB256.s: Indiana law now requires some tech contracts with state-related entities to include a promise that the contractor and its subcontractors are not barred persons. It also sets rules for people tied to hostile foreign countries, limits certain state benefits and property purchases by some foreign-linked people and businesses, and adds new school reporting and admission rules for foreign students. The law also repeals older rules on foreign ownership of farm land.

IN-2026-SB261.s: The law renames "criminal mischief" as "criminal vandalism." It moves several related crimes into that section, including damage to certain facilities, cemeteries, railroads, and caves, while keeping the same penalties and defenses. It also changes the law on throwing away trash in a cave and makes other related wording changes.

IN-2026-SB270.s: The law requires state officials to score townships outside Marion County and makes some higher-scoring townships merge with other townships or, in some cases, reorganize with a city or town. It sets steps and deadlines for choosing the new local government, creates a short-term government until new officials are elected in 2030, and keeps township assessor offices in place during a merger. It also changes reporting on fire protection, lets some counties move township assessor duties to the county assessor in limited cases, and became Public Law 134 on March 5, 2026.

IN-2026-SB271.s: Indiana law would treat telecommunications network wire as valuable metal for rules on metal dealers. It would bar people from selling or trying to sell that wire, and bar dealers from buying or trying to buy it, unless set conditions are met. It would also move the criminal penalties into the criminal code and let people seek money damages in court for losses from a violation. It became Public Law 142 on March 5, 2026.

IN-2026-SB277.s: The bill changes how the Indiana Department of Environmental Management and its review board work. It limits the department from using some federal risk values by themselves and makes changes to permits, hearings, reports, fees, water pollution, and solid and hazardous waste rules. It also repeals some programs and offices and became Public Law 135 on March 5, 2026.

IN-2026-SB282.s: Indiana's new law sets rules for drug compounding, which is making certain medicines in smaller batches, and asks state agencies to report on its risks and benefits. Starting January 1, 2027, medical spas must register with the Indiana medical licensing board, name a responsible practitioner, report serious harm events, and follow rules for ads and where services can be given. The board must also keep a public list of registered medical spas.

IN-2026-SB285.s: The law requires the Indiana housing and community development authority to set rules for who can be included in its federal homeless housing grant requests, and it requires grant recipients to send yearly reports. It also defines "gravely disabled" for involuntary commitment, which is when someone can be held for mental health treatment. The law bans camping, sleeping, or long-term shelter on state or local government land unless the use is allowed by law, and it sets rules for police response and possible misdemeanor charges in some cases. It also requires local police to report street-camping arrests and limits local policies that block enforcement of bans on public camping, while still allowing programs that offer housing or shelter instead of a ticket or arrest.

IN-2026-SB291.s: The law creates a way to keep certain personal details of protected judges out of public records kept by government agencies. It lets people sue a public agency that does not remove that information. It also changes court security by letting the Supreme Court and Court of Appeals appoint court marshals and deputies to help keep courts safe, with limited police powers and some legal protection for actions taken on the job.

IN-2026-SB293.s: Indiana passed a law about pharmacist licenses. It removes one exam step for some pharmacists who want a license through reciprocity, and it says an applicant must pass the North American Pharmacist Licensure Examination to qualify for a pharmacist license. The law also changes or cancels some state rules and makes technical updates.

IN-2026-SB4.s: The law requires a fiscal impact review for all governor executive orders within seven days, instead of only disaster emergency orders. It also lowers the cost trigger for state review of some proposed rules to more than $500,000 over two years, and changes the Pokagon Indiana Education Fund so it can pay public and private Indiana colleges and universities. Starting July 1, 2028, it changes how counties can help fund community mental health centers, adds rules for where some services may be given, and asks for more items in annual reports. It also lets the budget agency use some state money for child care vouchers, with budget committee review, and calls for a wider study of court fees and fines.

IN-2026-SB5.s: Indiana made this bill law. It lets the alcohol and tobacco commission refuse, suspend, or revoke a retailer’s permit if the licensed place becomes a public nuisance or is tied to certain crimes or banned conduct. It also lets the commission chair temporarily suspend a retail alcohol permit in some serious cases, and requires quick notice and a hearing within three business days.

IN-2026-SB6.s: The law adds notice and meeting steps before a city-owned utility can condemn land for a water or wastewater main outside the city or its current service area. It must mail written notices to affected landowners and the county plan commission, and post project details on its website and the county's website. A landowner or plan commission can ask for a meeting within 30 days, and the utility may move ahead after it meets the notice rules. Starting in 2027, the state utility regulator must report delays, complaints, and any action it takes.

IN-2026-SB71.s: This act changes several probate and guardianship rules in Indiana. It creates a task force to study updates to the guardianship code, and it makes changes for how property and money for minors can be handled, including some payments or transfers without a court order. It also updates rules for powers of attorney, trusts, and certain agreements tied to a family member’s home. It became Public Law 105 on March 5, 2026.

IN-2026-SB76.s: The law expands state rules on immigration matters for police, jails, schools, hospitals, and employers. It lets the attorney general defend certain public agencies or colleges in some lawsuits, and it requires jails and judges to record and act on immigration detainer requests, which are requests to hold someone for immigration authorities. It also says employers may not knowingly hire or keep an unauthorized alien, and it starts a new hospital report on patient ID for Medicaid cases beginning January 1, 2027. The bill became Public Law 106 on March 5, 2026.

IN-2026-SB78.s: The law changes rules for school policies on wireless devices like phones in Indiana schools and charter schools. It requires the state education department to publish a model policy and guidance for how to use it. It also gives schools and school staff some protection from civil lawsuits when they act in good faith to follow the policy, with exceptions.

IN-2026-SB80.s: The bill updates the Indiana Code by fixing technical conflicts from recent law changes and moving some definition sections so they can be organized and expanded later. It also makes matching cross-reference updates. It became Public Law 145 and makes no substantive change to the law.

IN-2026-SB88.s: The law changes Indiana’s good citizenship lessons and adds the Classic Learning Test to some references to college entrance exams. State colleges and universities must treat that test the same as the ACT or SAT when they use it for admission rules. The state education department must also list schools where outside students can take certain exams and make that list easy to find on its website.

IN-2026-SB91.s: This law changes rules for syringe exchange programs run by approved groups. It bars fixed sites from being within 1,000 feet of certain places, adds program rules, and lets the Indiana Department of Health deny, suspend, or revoke a group’s yearly registration for violations. It also stops these programs from giving out chemical reagents or precursors and extends the program’s end date to July 1, 2031.
